### R

```{r}
#| label: basin-iterates-r
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Plot of the double-well function x to the fourth minus 2 x squared
#|   for x from -1.6 to 1.6, a grey W-shaped curve with minima of -1
#|   at x of -1 and 1 and a local maximum of 0 at x of 0.
#|   Points mark the gradient descent iterates from six starting values,
#|   three positive and three negative.
#|   Positive starts, drawn as blue circles, slide down the right well to 1.
#|   Negative starts, drawn as orange triangles,
#|   slide down the left well to -1.
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 5
# Uses basin_step_bs and basin_starts_bs from the example above.
basin_cost_bf <- function(x) x^4 - 2 * x^2
basin_iterates_bf <- function(x0, step, n_steps) {
  x <- numeric(n_steps + 1)
  x[1] <- x0
  for (i in seq_len(n_steps)) {
    x[i + 1] <- x[i] - step * (4 * x[i]^3 - 4 * x[i])
  }
  x
}
basin_runs_bf <- lapply(
  basin_starts_bs[1:6], basin_iterates_bf,
  step = basin_step_bs, n_steps = 30
)
basin_paths_bf <- data.frame(
  x = unlist(basin_runs_bf),
  side = rep(
    ifelse(basin_starts_bs[1:6] > 0, "start above 0", "start below 0"),
    each = 31
  )
)
basin_paths_bf$cost <- basin_cost_bf(basin_paths_bf$x)
ggplot2::ggplot(basin_paths_bf, ggplot2::aes(x, cost)) +
  ggplot2::geom_function(
    fun = basin_cost_bf, colour = "grey60", xlim = c(-1.6, 1.6)
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    ggplot2::aes(colour = side, shape = side), alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("start above 0" = "#0072B2", "start below 0" = "#D55E00")
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "x", y = "f(x)", colour = NULL, shape = NULL) +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: basin-iterates-python
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Plot of the double-well function x to the fourth minus 2 x squared
#|   for x from -1.6 to 1.6, a grey W-shaped curve with minima of -1
#|   at x of -1 and 1 and a local maximum of 0 at x of 0.
#|   Points mark the gradient descent iterates from six starting values,
#|   three positive and three negative.
#|   Positive starts, drawn as blue circles, slide down the right well to 1.
#|   Negative starts, drawn as orange triangles,
#|   slide down the left well to -1.
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 5
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

def basin_cost_bf(x):
    return x ** 4 - 2 * x ** 2

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 4), layout="constrained")
grid_bf = np.linspace(-1.6, 1.6, 321)
ax.plot(grid_bf, basin_cost_bf(grid_bf), color="grey")
for start in basin_starts_bs[:6]:
    x = [start]
    for _ in range(30):
        x.append(basin_next_bs(x[-1]))
    x = np.array(x)
    above = start > 0
    ax.plot(x, basin_cost_bf(x), linestyle="", alpha=0.7,
            color="#0072B2" if above else "#D55E00",
            marker="o" if above else "^",
            label=("start above 0" if above else "start below 0")
            if abs(start) == 0.1 else None)
ax.set_xlabel("x")
ax.set_ylabel("f(x)")
fig.legend(loc="outside lower center", ncol=2)
plt.show()
```

:::

[Gradient descent](#def-gradient-descent)
with [step length](#def-gradient-descent) $`r basin_step_bs`$
on the double-well [function](functions.qmd#def-function)
of @exm-basin-of-attraction,
from six starting [values](functions.qmd#def-value).
Each run settles at the [local minimizer](algebra-basics.qmd#def-local-minimizer)
on its own side of the [local maximizer](#def-local-maximizer) at $0$.

:::
